questions.question_text:
The point $(4, -7)$ lies on the graph of $y = f(x)$.
What are the coordinates of the corresponding point on the graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$?

options.why: Negated the coordinates instead of interchanging their positions across the line $y = x$.
Negated and swapped coordinates rather than simply swapping $x$ and $y$.
Kept the coordinates unchanged instead of reflecting across $y = x$.

questions.solution_text:
Reflect $(x, y)$ in the line $y = x$ by swapping coordinates:
$(4, -7) \to (-7, 4)$

questions.question_text:
For an invertible function $f(x)$, it is given that $f(-3) = 5$ and $f(2) = 8$.
What is the value of $f^{-1}(5) + f^{-1}(8)$?

options.why: Added the output values $5 + 8$ instead of evaluating the inverse outputs $-3 + 2$.
Added $3 + (-2)$ due to sign errors when reversing the function values.
Subtracted the inputs $-3 - 2$ instead of adding $-3 + 2$.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = f(x)$ has an $x$-intercept at $(6, 0)$ and a $y$-intercept at $(0, -9)$.
What are the intercepts of the inverse graph $y = f^{-1}(x)$?

options.why: Kept the intercepts of the original function without swapping the axes.
Negated the coordinates instead of interchanging the $x$- and $y$-coordinates.
Swapped the axis names without interchanging the coordinate values.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = f(x)$ has a $y$-intercept at $(0, 3)$ and passes through $(4, 11)$.
What is the $x$-intercept of $y = f^{-1}(x)$?

options.why: Left the point as a $y$-intercept rather than reflecting it to an $x$-intercept.
Used the non-intercept point $(4, 11)$ instead of the $y$-intercept $(0, 3)$.
Negated the coordinate instead of swapping $x$ and $y$.

questions.solution_text: The $y$-intercept $(0, 3)$ reflects across $y = x$ to the $x$-intercept $(3, 0)$.

questions.question_text:
The function $y = f(x)$ has a vertical asymptote at $x = 5$ and a horizontal asymptote at $y = -2$.
What are the asymptotes of $y = f^{-1}(x)$?

options.why: Did not interchange horizontal and vertical asymptotes during reflection.
Negated the asymptote values instead of swapping their variables.
Both swapped and negated the signs of the asymptote equations incorrectly.

questions.solution_text:
Vertical asymptote $x = 5 \to$ horizontal asymptote $y = 5$
Horizontal asymptote $y = -2 \to$ vertical asymptote $x = -2$

questions.question_text:
The function $f(x) = e^{x+2} - 3$ has range $(-3, \infty)$.
What is the domain of $f^{-1}(x)$?

options.why: Confused the domain of $f^{-1}$ with the range of $f^{-1}$ (which is the domain of $f$).
Changed the sign of the lower boundary $-3$ to positive $3$.
Used the horizontal shift parameter $-2$ instead of the vertical range bound.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = f(x)$ passes through $(0, 1)$ and $(2, 5)$.
Which statement correctly describes the graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$?

options.text: It passes through $(1, 0)$ and $(5, 2)$ and is the reflection of $y = f(x)$ in $y = x$.
It passes through $(0, -1)$ and $(-2, -5)$ and is the reflection in the $x$-axis.
options.why: Reflected in the origin/axes rather than across the line $y = x$.

options.text: It passes through $(1, 0)$ and $(2, 5)$ without transforming all points.
options.why: Transformed the intercept but failed to transform the general point $(2, 5)$.

options.text: It passes through $(-1, 0)$ and $(-5, -2)$ by negating all coordinate values.
options.why: Negated coordinates instead of interchanging $x$ and $y$.

questions.question_text:
The function $f(x) = \sqrt{x - 1} + 2$ has an endpoint at $(1, 2)$.
What is the endpoint of the inverse function $y = f^{-1}(x)$?

options.why: Kept the endpoint unchanged without reflecting in $y = x$.
Negated the endpoint coordinates instead of swapping them.
Negated and swapped coordinates instead of only swapping.

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = f(x)$ has a point of inflection at $(3, -1)$ with a horizontal tangent.
What geometric feature does $y = f^{-1}(x)$ have at $(-1, 3)$?

options.text: A point of inflection with a vertical tangent
A point of inflection with a horizontal tangent
options.why: Failed to recognize that reflecting a horizontal line produces a vertical line.
Incorrectly changed an inflection point into an extremum.
Confused a vertical tangent with an asymptotic discontinuity.

questions.solution_text: Reflecting in $y = x$ transforms $(3, -1) \to (-1, 3)$ and transforms a horizontal tangent ($m = 0$) into a vertical tangent ($m \to \infty$).

questions.question_text:
The line $y = 4x - 6$ is tangent to the curve $y = f(x)$ at the point $(2, 2)$.
What is the equation of the tangent line to $y = f^{-1}(x)$ at $(2, 2)$?

options.why: Kept the original tangent line instead of finding the reciprocal gradient.
Used the negative reciprocal perpendicular gradient instead of the reciprocal.
Calculated the $y$-intercept incorrectly when substituting $(2, 2)$.

questions.solution_text:
Gradient of $f$ at $(2, 2)$ is $m = 4$.
Gradient of $f^{-1}$ at $(2, 2)$ is $m' = \dfrac{1}{4}$.
$y - 2 = \dfrac{1}{4}(x - 2)$
$y = \dfrac{1}{4}x + \dfrac{3}{2}$
